newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat tells Hebron settlers he wants peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat tells Hebron settlers he wants peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told Jewish settlers on arriving in Hebron on Sunday that he wanted peace.
He said his Palestinian Authority would respect its agreement with Israel which would lead to an independent Palestinian state with Arab East Jerusalem as its capital.
"I tell settlers we do not want confrontation," Arafat said in a short speech to thousands of cheering Hebronites. "We back a just peace," he said.
The 400 Jewish settlers in the heart of Hebron oppose the Israeli-PLO deal. Tension between them and Hebron's 100,000 Arabs has been high.

Arafat said Hebron was a springboard for further Israeli withdrawals in the West Bank. He said Israel would release Palestinian women prisoners in a few days followed by the eventual release of Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, the spiritual leader of the Islamic fundamentalist Hamas movement.
"Hebron is a springboard for what comes after...so that we can establish our independent Palestinian state, you have a big responsibility," Arafat said in Arabic.
"A promise is a promise, we will continue to Jerusalem," he said.
Arafat has made the same promise about "freeing" the 150,000 Palestinians in East Jerusalem in every city he has visited since arriving in Gaza in July 1994 to lead the self-rule Authority.
"I tell our people in Jerusalem they have to protect the Arab character of Jerusalem," he added, refering to Israel's vast buidling programme for Jews in the divided city.

Arafat said the Jewish state would free Palestinian women prisoners "within a few days." A U.S.-brokered peace deal between Arafat's Palestinian Authority and Israel reaffirmed an Israeli commitment made in a previous peace deal to release prisoners.
The release of prisoners, especially the blind, wheelchair-bound Yassin, would shore up Arafat's support on the Palestinian street, including in Hebron, a stronghold of Moslem militant activism.
"I tell the shabiba (activists) that your brother Sheikh Ahmed Yassin will be released soon," Arafat said.
